results.summary_before: This design implements a fuzzy search engine based on the bit-vector Levenshtein distance algorithm. It finds the closest matching word in a dictionary stored in external QSPI PSRAM, communicating with the host via SPI. The design requires a specific QSPI PSRAM PMOD that supports quad-mode operations and runs at half the clock speed of the chip. It is notable for being a hardware implementation of a string matching algorithm, with a provided client tool for testing.

results.summary_before: This project implements an 8-bit linear feedback shift register (LFSR) that generates a pseudo-random sequence. It accepts an 8-bit seed value and a write-enable signal to load the seed, and outputs the current LFSR state on eight output pins. The design is simple and requires no external hardware beyond reading the output pins. It can be used as a basic pseudo-random number generator.

results.summary_before: This project implements a single-layer perceptron in Verilog.
